# `m.futures.products`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Futures products: the specification of every product, the family of its contracts.

```python
m.futures.products(*, product_code=None, as_of=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `ProductCode`, `TradingVenue` and `Date` |
| `sort` | any REST field of the rows (see Massive fields below), or several separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc` |
| `filters` | `asset_class`, `asset_class_any_of`, `asset_sub_class`, `asset_sub_class_any_of`, `name`, `name_any_of`, `name_gt`, `name_gte`, `name_lt`, `name_lte`, `provider_id`, `sector`, `sector_any_of`, `sub_sector`, `sub_sector_any_of`, `trading_venue`, `trading_venue_any_of`, `trading_venue_gt`, `trading_venue_gte`, `trading_venue_lt`, `trading_venue_lte`, `type`, `type_any_of` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `product_code` | Only this product (`"ES"`) or these (`["ES", "NQ"]`); None for every product. A table of codes, in a `ProductCode` column, reads each code as if passed alone; a live one is followed by `fetch()` and re-read by each `poll()` cycle. |  |
| `as_of` | The day whose specifications to list; None for today. | The day to read the data as it stood on, as text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`. Leave it out for today's state. How far back you can go depends on your plan; this page's plan table says how much history each plan holds. |
| `sort` | Such as `"name"`; the endpoint sorts by `date`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | Needs `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Such as `{"sector": "precious"}` or `{"trading_venue": "XCME"}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Products (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Futures Basic | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Starter | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Developer | Updated daily, 5 years |
| Futures Advanced | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CME | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CBOT | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business NYMEX | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business COMEX | Updated daily, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AssetClass` | String | The asset class to which the product belongs. | REST |
| `AssetSubClass` | String | The asset sub-class to which the product belongs. | REST |
| `ClearingSymbol` | String | The clearing symbol assigned to this product by the exchange's clearing house. | REST |
| `ClearingVenue` | String | The exchange identifier for the clearing house that clears this product's contracts. | REST |
| `Date` | String | The day, YYYY-MM-DD, whose point-in-time state the row describes. | REST |
| `LastUpdated` | Instant | The date and time at which this product was last updated. | REST |
| `Name` | String | The full name of the product. | REST |
| `PriceQuotation` | String | The quoted price for this product. | REST |
| `ProductCode` | String | The identifier for the product. | REST |
| `ProviderId` | String | A unique identifier for the product assigned by the data provider. Can be used to distinguish products that share a product code. | REST |
| `Sector` | String | The sector to which the product belongs. | REST |
| `SettlementCurrencyCode` | String | The currency in which this product settles. | REST |
| `SettlementMethod` | String | The method of settlement for this product (Financially Settled or Deliverable). | REST |
| `SettlementType` | String | The type of settlement for this product. | REST |
| `StrategyType` | String | The strategy type for combo products (e.g. calendar, butterfly, strip). Null for single products. | REST |
| `SubSector` | String | The sub-sector to which the product belongs. | REST |
| `TradeCurrencyCode` | String | The currency in which this product's contracts trade. | REST |
| `TradingVenue` | String | The trading venue (MIC) for the exchange on which this product's contracts trade. | REST |
| `Type` | String | The type of product, one of 'single' or 'combo'. Leaving this filter blank will query for both 'single' and 'combo' types. | REST |
| `UnitOfMeasure` | String | The unit of measure for this product. | REST |
| `UnitOfMeasureQty` | double | The quantity of the unit of measure for this product. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
